subject: AWS/GCP marketplace cost mapping — follow up and next steps
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>
To: Elena Morales <emorales@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS/GCP marketplace cost mapping — follow up and next steps

Hi Elena — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and the asks we discussed so procurement can map this into the marketplace private-offer flow.

Key call takeaways (high level):
- You plan to route purchases via AWS Private Offers for US customers, with GCP Marketplace as a secondary sales path for some enterprise accounts.
- Expected steady-state monthly token consumption: approx 50M — 120M tokens/month (spikes during campaigns).
- Budget guidance: high-level range given as $750 — $1,000 per 1M tokens (targeting an initial committed unit price).
- Procurement timeline: procurement team evaluating Marketplace PO workflow next 2–3 weeks; contract/legal review to follow.

What we need from you to produce an initial marketplace PO price bridge:
1) Confirmation of primary marketplace (AWS vs GCP) and whether you require a private-offer or a net-new listing.
2) The target net unit price you want exposed in the PO (if you have a hard internal target).
3) A close estimate of monthly and annual token commitment horizons (e.g., 100M/mo x 12 months = 1.2B tokens).
4) Any procurement constraints: PO invoice cadence, purchase order number, or internal approval gates.

Attached: redwood-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet) — I added three mapping scenarios (no-commit/list-price, 12mo commit, 24mo commit + milestone discounts).

Next steps I propose:
- You share the procurement template and a PO owner contact.
- We produce a short cost-bridge doc that maps our hosted list price to an AWS Private Offer unit price and a parallel GCP quote.
- Schedule a 30-min procurement alignment call (suggested window: Tue/Wed next week).

Thanks — I’ll draft the bridge once we have the procurement template and the commit numbers.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Account Exec, Retail & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-pricing-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Elena Morales <emorales@acme-retail.com>

Date: 2027-05-09T18:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS/GCP marketplace cost mapping — follow up and next steps

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear recap. A few answers below and an attached procurement template.

Quick answers:
- Primary marketplace: AWS Private Offers for commercial customers in the US. We will use GCP Marketplace only for a small subset of enterprise deals where customers mandate GCP billing.
- Internal target net price: we are aiming at roughly $800 — $950 / 1M tokens as an internal target for the first year (we can be flexible if the economics are justified by commit / term).
- Expected commitment: planning scenario is 80M — 120M tokens/mo for year 1 with expected 20% growth in year 2. Rough annual baseline = ~1.2B tokens.
- Procurement constraints: PO cadence is quarterly invoicing; they prefer a 12-month committed term.

Attached: acme-procurement-template.pdf (procurement template) — includes fields you’ll need for the AWS PO (billing contact, PO number format, SOW references).

Two asks for your side:
1) Can you show a simple mapping showing hosted list price -> AWS PO unit price at (a) no-commit, (b) 12mo commit 1.2B, (c) 24mo commit 2.4B?
2) Any nuance with token accounting for caching or burst credits we should be aware of?

Happy to hop on procurement call next week — I’ll loop in our procurement lead once we have your proposed mapping.

Best,
Elena
Director, Data Products — Acme Retail
[Attachment: acme-procurement-template.pdf (pdf)]

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-05-10T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS/GCP marketplace cost mapping — follow up and next steps

Elena — thanks for the numbers and the template. Below is a short cost-bridge explaining how list pricing maps to marketplace private-offer unit price and where the levers are. I’ll convert this into a one-page PDF for procurement after you confirm the commitment size.

How we map list -> PO unit price (short):
- Baseline (hosted list): our standard hosted unit price for the model family you’re evaluating (high-throughput gen) is $950 / 1M tokens. This is the public list unit for on-demand API.
- Marketplace private offer mechanics (AWS): AWS PO shows a per-unit price that AWS will charge customers; the PO price can be set lower than list to reflect term/commit discounts, but AWS fees (platform/transaction) and any marketplace percentage adjustments must be applied before we translate to our net receipt.
- Quick example (illustrative):
  * No commit (on-demand): list = $950 / 1M, PO typically mirrors list -> customer pays $950.
  * 12mo commit (1.2B tokens): suggested PO unit price = $760 / 1M (net to Redwood after marketplace fees ~ $725) — this assumes ~20% gross discount vs list for a 12mo, 1.2B commitment.
  * 24mo commit (2.4B tokens): suggested PO unit price = $680 / 1M (net to Redwood ~ $650) — reflects deeper term discount and reserve-capacity pricing.

GCP/Azure notes:
- GCP Marketplace uses an invoiced contract path; we can replicate the net unit pricing but the billing flows differ (GCP invoices the customer and we receive settlement on a schedule). Azure has a separate commercial marketplace flow; discounts and listing requirements vary by region.

Token accounting caveats:
- Prefix caching / local KV cache: cached tokens consumed from Redwood capacity still count against the committed usage unless explicitly excluded in the contract; we typically model a 5–10% reduction in billable tokens due to caching optimizations for steady-state interactive workloads.
- Burst credits: we can include an agreed burst buffer (e.g., 20% additional monthly tokens) that is billed if used at a list or agreed overage rate.

Next steps / ask list:
- Please confirm: (A) pick the commit scenario you want us to price (no-commit / 12mo / 24mo) and (B) confirm PO owner & preferred procurement call times.
- We’ll produce a one-pager cost-bridge + a draft AWS PO unit price proposal and share with your procurement team.

I’ll loop in Marissa for the PO setup checklist after you confirm the scenario.

Thanks,
Naomi
Account Exec, Retail & Marketplaces
Redwood Inference

Naomi / team — quick internal note with negotiation levers and a suggested starting structure before we send the bridge to Acme: 

Negotiation levers to highlight:
- Commit size & term (primary driver of net price).
- Billing cadence (quarterly invoicing helps Acme cashflow but increases our working capital; offset with a slightly higher net unit price or prepayment credit).
- Regional pricing: offer US-heavy pricing for AWS PO, keep GCP as a separate SKU for customers that require it.
- SLA / uptime credits: limit exposure to tiered credits; treat as a separate credit ledger.

Suggested public starting point to test with procurement (internal):
- 12mo committed: 1.2B tokens/year -> Net target to Redwood ~ $720 / 1M (customer-facing PO price ~ $760 / 1M to account for AWS fees).
- Optional add-on: 20% burst buffer per month billed at list-overage rate ($950/1M).
- Upsell path: year 2 growth breakpoints (1.5B -> additional 5% discount).

If Naomi confirms the 12mo scenario, I’ll draft the pricing lines Marissa needs for the PO.

-Ben
Senior Account Director, Marketplaces
Redwood Inference
